title: Relative smooth tangent module and torus weights under base change
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $r\geq0$. An $A$-group scheme means a scheme over $X$ with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying associativity, unit and inverse diagrams, as in [def-sc-group-scheme] with this base in place of a field. Put $T=\mathbf G_{m,A}^r=\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$, $M=\mathbf Z^r$, where $A[M]=A[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$, $e^m=\prod_jz_j^{m_j}$, and the group law is multiplication of units. Write $\chi_m:T\to\mathbf G_{m,A}$ for the character $e^m$. Let $G$ be any smooth affine finite-type $A$-group scheme, with an action of $T$ by $A$-group automorphisms. Define $\mathfrak g=\ker(G(A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to G(A))$, with addition given by the group law and scalar multiplication given by $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$. Then $\mathfrak g$ is a finite projective $A$-module (a direct summand of a finite free module). The differentiated action is an $A$-linear coaction $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g\otimes_A A[M]$. For $\mathfrak g_m=\{v:\rho(v)=v\otimes e^m\}$ one has $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{m\in M}\mathfrak g_m$, only finitely many summands are nonzero, and each summand is finite projective. For every commutative $A$-algebra $B$, the natural tangent comparison $B\otimes_A\mathfrak g\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker(G_B(B[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to G_B(B))$ is $B$-linear and carries $B\otimes_A\mathfrak g_m$ isomorphically onto the $m$-weight summand for the full $T_B$-coaction. These comparisons are compatible with successive algebra extensions. No reductivity, connectedness, local-ring hypothesis, or restriction on residue characteristic is required.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, background on Lie functors, printed p.2; introduction to Section 4, printed p.107, M-graded vector bundle and arbitrary base change. General smooth tangent module uses the smooth cotangent bundle at the identity; the coaction argument is the same for any torus action. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and let $u:C\to A$ be the identity section on coordinates. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] to the given smooth affine structure morphism: $A\to C$ is a smooth ring map. By [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $\Omega=\Omega_{C/A}$ is a direct summand of $C^N$ for some finite $N$. Put $Q=A\otimes_{C,u}\Omega$. Tensor the inclusion and retraction of this summand with $A$; their composite remains the identity, so $Q$ is a direct summand of $A^N$. The identification $A\otimes_C C^N=A^N$ sends $a\otimes(c_j)_j$ to $(a u(c_j))_j$, with inverse $(a_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j a_j\otimes e_j$. Thus $Q$ is finite projective.

source.place: Tag 00T2, definition-smooth; affine input Tags 01V6 (morphisms.tex, lemma-smooth-characterize) and 02H6 (more-morphisms.tex, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth).

proof.text: For any commutative $A$-algebra $R$, an $R$-valued tangent point of $G_R$ is uniquely a map $C\to R[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ of the form $c\mapsto u(c)+\epsilon D(c)$, with $u(c)$ now mapped into $R$. Multiplying two such values says exactly $D(cc')=u(c)D(c')+u(c')D(c)$; additivity and $D(A)=0$ are the other algebra-map conditions. By the universal property of $\Omega$, these derivations are $C$-linear maps $\Omega\to R$, where $C$ acts through $u$. The tensor universal property identifies these with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(Q,R)$: a functional $f$ corresponds to $D(c)=f(1\otimes dc)$, and the inverse sends $a\otimes\omega$ to $a\,\widetilde D(\omega)$. Both formulas commute with $R\to R'$. In particular the tangent set in the item is $Q^*=\operatorname{Hom}_A(Q,A)$.

source.place: Tag 00RO, lemma-universal-omega; the first-order coefficient calculation and tensor adjunction are written out here.

proof.text: This identification gives exactly the operations in the question. On coordinates write the multiplication pullback $\mu^*(c)=\sum_i c_i\otimes c_i'\in C\otimes_A C$. Multiplying the tangent points belonging to $D,E$ gives first-order coefficient $\sum_i D(c_i)u(c_i')+u(c_i)E(c_i')=D(c)+E(c)$: the two unit identities say $\sum_i c_i u(c_i')=c=\sum_i u(c_i)c_i'$. The constant coefficient is $u(c)$ and the product of two $\epsilon$ terms is zero. The change $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$ changes $D$ to $aD$. Hence the group kernel is an $A$-module with the required addition and scalar multiplication, and its identification with $Q^*$ is linear. The same computation works over every $R$.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, and the commutative-algebra tensor pushout; elementary first-order expansion of multiplication and its unit identities.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sf-finite-projective-dual] hold for the finite projective $A$-module $Q$ from step 1. Its dual $Q^*$ is therefore finitely generated and projective. By step 3 this is the module $\mathfrak g$ of the item. It is also explicitly a summand of a finite free module: dualize a chosen splitting $Q\xrightarrow{i}A^N\xrightarrow{s}Q$, obtaining $Q^*\xrightarrow{s^*}(A^N)^*\xrightarrow{i^*}Q^*$ with composite identity, and identify $(A^N)^*$ with $A^N$ by its coordinate functionals.

source.place: Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, termwise finite-projective duality; existing node is a Mathlib leaf.

proof.text:
Fix any commutative $A$-algebra $B$. Kähler base change gives $\Omega_{(B\otimes_A C)/B}\simeq (B\otimes_A C)\otimes_C\Omega$, carrying $d(1\otimes c)$ to $1\otimes dc$. Pullback by the identity $B\otimes_A C\to B$ gives $Q_B\simeq B\otimes_A Q$; the reassociation sends $b\otimes(a\otimes\omega)$ to $ba\otimes\omega$, and its inverse inserts $1$ in the middle. The natural dual comparison
$$B\otimes_A Q^*\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\otimes_A Q,B),\qquad b\otimes f\longmapsto(b'\otimes q\mapsto bb'f(q))$$
is invertible without flatness: choose $q_j=s(e_j)$ and $f_j=e_j^*i$ from step 4, so $q=\sum_j f_j(q)q_j$. Its inverse sends $F$ to $\sum_j F(1\otimes q_j)\otimes f_j$; the two composites are identities by this formula for $q$ and its dual $f=\sum_j f(q_j)f_j$. With step 2 this proves the required tangent comparison $\Phi_B$. Its value at $b\otimes D$ has coefficient $D_B(b'\otimes c)=bb'D(c)$, so it is the natural comparison and is $B$-linear.

source.place: Tag 00RV, lemma-differentials-base-change; finite-summand dual-basis calculation given explicitly, not an appeal to Hom base change without hypotheses.

proof.text: For $A\to B\xrightarrow{h}B'$, compare $\Phi_{B'}$ with extension of $\Phi_B$ using $B'\otimes_B(B\otimes_A\mathfrak g)\simeq B'\otimes_A\mathfrak g$, $b'\otimes(b\otimes D)\mapsto b'h(b)\otimes D$. On $c\in C$ both resulting tangent points have coefficient $b'h(b)D(c)$. On $b''\otimes c\in B'\otimes_A C$ multiply this by $b''$. Pure tensors generate, so the comparisons agree. The map for $A\to A$ is the identity by the same formula.

source.place: Section 00CV, section-tensor-product, generator formulas; explicit verification of successive scalar extensions.

proof.text: Put $H=A[M]$. The action $a:T\times_A G\to G$ gives on coordinates $a^*:C\to H\otimes_A C$. The generic point $t\in T(H)$ is the identity map of $H$. Apply $t$ to the scalar extension of $e+\epsilon D$ and use $\Phi_H^{-1}$ from step 5, followed by interchange of tensor factors; this defines $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g\otimes_A H$. More explicitly, if $a^*(c)=\sum_i h_i\otimes c_i$, the resulting tangent coefficient at $c$ is $\sum_i h_iD(c_i)$. It is a derivation at $u_H$ because the action is an algebra map and fixes the identity. This formula is $A$-linear in $D$, proving linearity of $\rho$. It also proves compatibility with any algebra map $H\to R$: applying that map gives the differentiated action of the corresponding element of $T(R)$.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, coordinate description of an action; the tangent-coaction construction for the given action is an explicit calculation here.

proof.text: The identity element of $T$ is the counit $\varepsilon:H\to A$, so the coefficient formula of step 7 and the identity-action diagram give $(1\otimes\varepsilon)\rho=1$. Over $H\otimes_A H$, let $t_1,t_2$ be the two generic elements. Applying first $t_2$ and then $t_1$ to $e+\epsilon D$ gives the same point as applying $t_1t_2$, by the given action diagram. Under the invertible tangent comparisons of steps 5–6 these two coefficients are respectively $(\rho\otimes1)\rho(D)$ and $(1\otimes\Delta)\rho(D)$, with $\Delta(e^m)=e^m\otimes e^m$. Thus $\rho$ satisfies both coaction identities as actual module maps. This comparison uses generic points, not only points over residue fields.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, proof comparing the two action composites; the same generic-coordinate comparison applied to first-order coefficients.

proof.text: Use the existing ring-coaction theorem on the square-zero $A$-algebra $E=A\oplus\mathfrak g$, with $(a,v)(b,w)=(ab,aw+bv)$. Extend $\rho$ by $\theta(a,v)=a\otimes1+\rho(v)$ in $E\otimes_A H$, with the two terms in the constant and square-zero summands. This is an algebra homomorphism: multiplying images gives constant part $ab$ and module part $a\rho(w)+b\rho(v)$, since the product of two square-zero terms is zero. Step 8 gives its counit and coassociativity. The ring $A$, group $M$, algebra $E$, and $\theta$ therefore satisfy [lem-sfb-group-algebra-coaction-grading]. Restrict its unique finite homogeneous expansion of $(0,v)$ to the square-zero summand. Coefficient projections preserve that summand, so this gives the unique expansion $v=\sum_m v_m$ with $\rho(v_m)=v_m\otimes e^m$. Thus the sum map $\bigoplus_m\mathfrak g_m\to\mathfrak g$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm; arbitrary-base/group-algebra form is precisely the cited existing node; square-zero specialization written out.

proof.text: Choose finite module generators $v_1,\ldots,v_s$ of $\mathfrak g$. The union $F$ of the finite supports of their homogeneous expansions is finite. Every linear combination of the $v_i$ has support in $F$, so $\mathfrak g_m=0$ for $m\notin F$. Let $p_m$ be the coefficient projection and $j_m$ the inclusion of $\mathfrak g_m$. Uniqueness of the expansion gives $p_mj_m=1$ and $j_mp_mj_m=j_m$. Since $\mathfrak g$ is a summand of $A^N$, composing its inclusion and retraction with $j_m,p_m$ exhibits $\mathfrak g_m$ as a summand of the same finite free module. It is finite projective, including when it is zero.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, coefficient projections; finite-support and finite-summand arguments are explicit consequences.

proof.text: For arbitrary $B$, tensor the maps $j_m,p_m$ for the finite set $F$. They still satisfy $p_mj_n=\delta_{mn}$ and $\sum_{m\in F}j_mp_m=1$, so $B\otimes_A\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{m\in F}(B\otimes_A\mathfrak g_m)$ with each tensor inclusion injective. Steps 5 and 7 show that $\Phi_B$ intertwines the coaction with the scalar extension of $\rho$: on the coefficient belonging to $b\otimes D$ at $a_B^*(b'\otimes c)$ both give $bb'\sum_i h_iD(c_i)$, now in $B[M]$, whenever $a^*(c)=\sum_i h_i\otimes c_i$. Hence each displayed summand has coaction $w\mapsto w\otimes e^m$. Conversely write a vector as $\sum_{n\in F}w_n$ in this decomposition. If its coaction is $w\otimes e^m$, comparison of the free Laurent basis coefficients gives $w_n=0$ for $n\ne m$ and $w=w_m$ (or $w=0$ if $m\notin F$). Coefficient comparison remains valid over every $B$: the coefficient maps on $B[M]$ give inverse maps between $W\otimes_B B[M]$ and finitely supported families in any $B$-module $W$, by $w\otimes\sum b_n e^n\mapsto(b_nw)_n$ and $(w_n)_n\mapsto\sum w_n\otimes e^n$. This proves exact identification with the full coaction weight module, including nonflat and zero $B$.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, coefficient comparison; base-change proof uses split maps and Laurent coefficients, with no kernel-exactness assumption.

proof.text: Finally, the tower comparison of step 6 restricts to $b'\otimes(b\otimes v_m)\mapsto b'h(b)\otimes v_m$ on every weight summand, because both coactions on this vector are its tensor with $e^m$. These pure tensors generate each summand. Thus the weight comparisons as well as the tangent comparisons are compatible with successive algebra extensions. If $r=0$ only weight $0$ occurs; if $\mathfrak g=0$ all summands and maps are zero. No step used reductivity, connectedness, localness, or a residue-characteristic assumption.

source.place: Section 00CV, section-tensor-product; explicit tower formula restricted to the split summands.
